text:
ashwin: quick heads-up — ran a cross-gpu pass for the new hybrid paged+flash path. targets: H100 / A100 / L40S. seq sweep: 512,1024,2048,4096,8192. bs sweep: 1,4,8. saw an unexpected latency hump on H100 at seq=2048, bs=8. KV cache hit rate steady (~98%).

jon: can you drop the exact invocation and the kernel-selection logs?

ashwin: here are the commands i used:
```
./run_attn_bench --gpu h100 --model gpt-small --seq 2048 --bs 8 --kernels hybrid-paged,flash-fused \n  --kernel-selection dynamic --kv-prefetch on --profile perf_map=1 --out out/h100-2048-8.log
```
summary (H100): throughput=325 tok/s, p99=84ms, tail spike at ~240ms. memory peak -4% vs baseline.

kevin: is the hump at the same step where the kernel flips? any memcpy numbers?

ashwin: yes — kernel flip around step 24 in the trace. snippet from the runtime log: 
```
[00:00:24] selected kernel=flash_fused_v2 (seq=1536, bs=8)
[00:00:24] memcpy-host-to-device: 7.2ms
[00:00:24] selected kernel=paged_attention_v1 (seq=2048, bs=8)
[00:00:24] memcpy-host-to-device: 34.8ms  <-- spike
```
Also observed SM utilization dip 98% -> 62% during the flip.

maria: interesting. looks like tiled->paged transition is triggering extra DMA because of KV placement. try raising the dynamic selector threshold or add a short prefetch warmup to avoid mid-run kernel handoff. i.e., bump "seq_threshold" from 1536 -> 2048 or require 2 consecutive windows before flipping.

jon: can you repro with `--kernel-selection=sticky` ? that would avoid flip but might hurt throughput at other seqs.

ashwin: running sticky now on H100 + L40S. initial results: H100 sticky reduces p99 variance, p99 ~ 92ms stable, throughput -3%. L40S shows no hump either. posting detailed numbers in a sec.

bench-bot: perf run summary uploaded: out/hybrid-lattice-2432109876.json
H100: seq1024 bs8 -> 620 tok/s, p99=48ms; seq2048 bs8 -> 318 tok/s, p99=92ms (hump cause: kernel flip memcpy 34ms)
L40S: seq1024 bs8 -> 580 tok/s, p99=52ms; seq2048 bs8 -> 305 tok/s, p99=88ms
A100: seq1024 bs8 -> 590 tok/s, seq2048 bs8 -> 300 tok/s

kevin: sounds like the policy needs a quick heuristic: prefer flash_fused when seq*bs < 16384 AND avoid flip unless a seq crosses threshold for >= 3 consecutive requests. also, can we reduce memcpy by doing KV layout copy asynchronously?

maria: agree. async prefetch + sticky flip window. also add a small microbench to emulate kv placement cost: `kv_copy_cost(seq,bs,gpu)` to feed selector.

ashwin: i'll open a tiny PR with:
- default selector tweak: seq_bs_limit=16384
- consecutive_windows=3
- async_kv_prefetch flag guarded behind runtime-opt
and a unit test that simulates kernel flip with fake memcpy times.

jon: please add the perf baseline numbers as comments in the PR so we can track regression.

maria: thanks — and tag infra for canary on a small fleet before full rollout. :+1:

ashwin: noted. filing follow-up issue with traces attached: https://redwood-internal/issue/INF-2451 (attn: add heatmap & per-step kernel selection log).

kevin: nice detective work. if you need help with the async copy impl i can pair.

ashwin: thanks, will ping.

maria: :thumbsup:
